court: In the High Court of Madras†
judges_raw: (Before S.M. Subramaniam and K. Surender, JJ.)
respondents: Government of Tamilnadu Rep. by its Secretary to Government School Education Department and Others … Respondent(s).
To set aside and review the Order dated 05.03.2021, in W.A. 1118 of 2019
advocates: For Respondent(s): Mr. K.H. Ravikumar, Govt. Advocte for R 1 to R 4
judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

S.M. Subramaniam, J.:— The judgment dated 5-3-2021 passed in W.A. No. 1118 of 2019 is sought to be reviewed in the present petition.

2. Mr R. Saseetharan, learned counsel for the petitioner would mainly contend that there are two judgments by the same Bench taking different views and therefore, the judgment in the Writ appeal is to be reviewed. He would rely on the judgment of the same Division Bench dated 16-10-2020 passed in the case of Secretary to Government, Department of School Education, Fort St. George, Chennai v. G. Rufus David, where the State appeal came to be dismissed. However, in W.A. No. 1118 of 2019 dated 5-3-2021, the State appeal is allowed. Taking the said stand, he would submit that the present review petition is to be considered.

3. Per contra, the learned government advocate would oppose stating that the issues are no more res integra and in respect of the earlier judgment of the year 2020 in the case of Rufus David was considered by the subsequent Division Bench, by relying on the judgment of the Supreme Court and the State appeal was allowed. Thus, the issues are no more res integra. In this regard, the learned government advocate would rely on the subsequent judgment in the case of S.K. Kannan v. Director of School Education dated 15-7-2022 in W.A.(MD). No. 627/2022, wherein the appeal filed by the employee was dismissed. Thereafter, another Division Bench in W.A.(MD). No. 686 of 2022 dated 24-3-2025 elaboratedly considered all these judgments including the judgment of the year 2020 relied on by the petitioner i.e. Rufus David's case and allowed the State Appeal. Paragraph Nos. 12 and 13 of the said judgment reads as under:

12. The learned counsel appearing for the respondent submitted that recently the learned Single Judge of this Court, in R. Lilly Theras v. the Government of Tamil Nadu, vide order dated 14-3-2024, has followed the judgment rendered in W.A. No. 3868 of 2019, The Secretary to State Government v. G. Rufus David, and has allowed the writ petition extending the benefit of FR and refixation of pay scale. With great respect to the learned Single Judge, it is noted that though the judgment of S.K. Kannan v. The Director of School Education, in W.A.(MD) No. 627 of 2022 was brought to the notice of the learned Single Judge, he had observed that the dictum laid in the S.K. Kannan judgment will not apply to the case in hand. He had distinguished the case under his consideration with that of the fact in S.K. Kannan's case. According to this Court, since the facts in S.K. Kannan's case as well as the S. Arulmani case and L. Esakkiraj case, are identical to the facts of the case in hand and bound by the judgments rendered by the equallent strength, allow the writ appeal following the three judgments which is based on the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Palure Bhaskar Rao Etc. Etc. v. P. Ramaseshaiah, (2017) 5 SCC 783.

13. We hold that the learned Single Judge has erred in allowing the writ of mandamus ignoring the consistent view of the Division Bench judgment, liable to be set aside.

4. In view of the said factum, the petitioner has not made out any error apparent warranting interference by this Court. Consequently, the Review Application stands dismissed. No costs.
